advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Pass an exclude pattern (or filter vendored/generated/ignored paths) to lizard.analyze so aggregate CCN is deterministic and excludes non-source trees.
evidence: src/rebar/metrics/analyzers/lizard_complexity.py:33: `files = _file_complexity(lizard.analyze([str(root)]), root)` — no exclude_pattern / lans / exts passed; lizard by default does not honor .gitignore
Contrast scc_loc which shells to scc that respects gitignore by default (src/rebar/metrics/analyzers/scc_loc.py:40)

The docstring promises 'deterministic' results but scanning vendored trees makes aggregates environment-dependent (module docstring at lizard_complexity.py:14: 'deterministic, per-function cyclomatic complexity')
advisory.finding: `lizard.analyze([str(root)])` scans the entire directory tree with no exclude/gitignore filtering, so vendored/generated directories (node_modules, .venv, build outputs, .git) are counted, inflating aggregate CCN and making results non-deterministic across hosts. The sibling scc analyzer relies on scc's default gitignore-respecting behavior.
scenarios: A repo with committed vendored JS (node_modules) or a local .venv gets its total_ccn/functions dominated by third-party code
CI vs local produce different aggregates depending on which build/venv dirs are present

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the outside-repo case fail-open (skip the file or return Unavailable) consistent with scc_loc, rather than raising an uncaught ValueError.
evidence: src/rebar/metrics/analyzers/lizard_complexity.py:49-51: `except ValueError as exc: raise ValueError(f"lizard reported a file outside repository: {location}") from exc` — propagates to caller

scc_loc converts the same outside-repo condition into Unavailable: `_relative_location` raises ValueError (scc_loc.py:105) but analyze catches `(TypeError, ValueError)` and returns `_unavailable(...)` (scc_loc.py:54-55)
The analyze() return type is `AnalyzerResult | Unavailable`, implying a non-raising / fail-open contract that this path violates
advisory.finding: An outside-repository file raises an uncaught ValueError that aborts the entire analyzer, unlike the sibling scc analyzer which converts the equivalent condition into an Unavailable result (fail-open). A single stray/symlinked file makes the whole complexity pass throw instead of degrading gracefully.
scenarios: A symlink inside repo_root pointing outside the tree causes lizard to report an out-of-tree resolved path, aborting the analyzer with an exception
Any single problematic file aborts complexity for the whole repo rather than being skipped or reported as Unavailable

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that feeds a lizard file record whose filename resolves outside `repo_root` and asserts `analyze` raises `ValueError` with the 'lizard reported a file outside repository' message.
evidence: src/rebar/metrics/analyzers/lizard_complexity.py:50-53: `except ValueError as exc:` -> `raise ValueError(f"lizard reported a file outside repository: {location}") from exc`

ABSENCE: search for 'outside repository' across tests/ returned no matches; the two new test files (test_lizard_complexity.py, test_lizard_complexity_heldout.py) only feed filenames UNDER `repo_root` (e.g. `repo_root / 'web' / 'choose.js'`) or an empty analysis, never a path outside the root
The four tests cover happy-path, real polyglot, missing-extra, and empty-analysis; none reaches the `relative_to` failure path
advisory.finding: The `_file_complexity` outside-repository error branch (raises `ValueError` with a specific message when `location.relative_to(repo_root)` fails) is untested; no test injects a lizard file record whose filename resolves outside the repo root, so this deliberate, observable error contract has no regression guard.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test to test_lizard_complexity_heldout.py that monkeypatches `guard_import` to return a fake lizard whose `analyze` yields a `SimpleNamespace(filename=str(tmp_path / 'elsewhere' / 'x.py'), function_list=[...])` outside `repo_root`, then asserts `pytest.raises(ValueError, match='outside repository')`.
